Dahāqīn—with either a ḍamma or a fatḥa on the dāl—is a Persian word that originally meant the head of a district and later came to refer to large landowners. Khān was originally a Turkish title meaning ruler, and later came to refer to a feudal prince.↩︎
For the land system and the condition of the peasants before the Arab conquest, see A. Christensen, Iran under the Sassanids, Arabic trans. Yaḥyā al-Khashshāb, Dār al-Fikr al-ʿArabī, Cairo.↩︎
